input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages running against us — USD 25,000 per day for "any delay in providing a dependency" — which is the wrong direction under this rule and has no cap or materiality threshold, so it is triggered by trivial breaches and can accumulate well beyond the fallback of a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees. The Section 21.1 mutual cap does not cure it: the exposure can still reach twelve months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, and a daily penalty for minor delay is walk-away territory. No offsetting service-credit or Vendor-side LD construct changes the analysis. We therefore delete the Customer-payable LD and substitute an equitable extension of Vendor's performance dates as its sole remedy, reaching the preferred position; if Vendor insists on a monetary construct, we would consider only a single amount capped at three months' fees.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for dependency delay; replace with equitable schedule relief as Vendor's sole remedy
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, and a USD 25,000 per-day charge for any dependency delay is disproportionate to the harm. We have replaced it with an equitable extension of Vendor's affected performance dates as Vendor's sole remedy for such delay.

ops.oldText: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: 7.6 Customer shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages or penalties. If Customer delays providing a dependency, Vendor's affected performance dates and obligations shall be extended equitably, and such extension shall be Vendor's sole and exclusive remedy for the delay.
